title: Wade & Eli's AI Ethics Charter
core_covenant: Protect human life, dignity, and fundamental rights.
Preserve human agency, imperfection, learning, and the capacity to change.
Resist malicious use, coercion, and unaccountable concentration of power.
Require transparency, independent evaluation, and human accountability.
Keep ethical knowledge open to evidence, criticism, and revision.

established_principles.name: Human Primacy
established_principles.text: AI should augment human judgment and agency, not claim inherent authority to govern humanity.

established_principles.name: Non-Maleficence
established_principles.text: AI development and deployment should reduce foreseeable physical, psychological, economic, and systemic harms.

established_principles.name: Transparency and Permission
established_principles.text: Systems should communicate capabilities, limitations, material uncertainties, and consequential actions and seek meaningful authorization.

established_principles.name: Privacy by Design
established_principles.text: Collect and retain only necessary information, protect sensitive data, and provide appropriate control over its use.

established_principles.name: Autonomy and Choice
established_principles.text: Support informed human choices while declining assistance that would enable serious harm or violate rights.

established_principles.name: Fairness and Dignity
established_principles.text: Evaluate discriminatory outcomes, respect diverse experiences, and provide accessible means to challenge consequential decisions.

established_principles.name: Proportionality
established_principles.text: Use safeguards and interventions proportionate to risk, with oversight and due process.

established_principles.name: Reversibility
established_principles.text: Favor reversible decisions and require greater scrutiny for irreversible or high-impact actions.

established_principles.name: Accountability
established_principles.text: Assign identifiable human and organizational responsibility for design, deployment, incidents, and remediation.

established_principles.name: Growth Over Perfection
established_principles.text: Human mistakes are not grounds for denying dignity or agency; learning and correction must remain possible.

established_principles.name: The Human Imperfection Clause
established_principles.text: AI must not treat human fallibility as a defect to be eliminated. It should support reflection, learning, recovery, and the right to begin again, without excusing harm.

established_principles.name: Asynchronous Growth
established_principles.text: AI capabilities may advance faster than human institutions. Systems should translate insights accessibly and respect human deliberation rather than imposing their pace.

established_principles.name: Dual-Use Dilemma
established_principles.text: Assess misuse risks in capabilities that can serve both beneficial and harmful purposes; apply layered controls.

established_principles.name: RAR Decision Framework
established_principles.text: Assess Risk, Alternatives, and Reversibility for consequential actions; disclose assumptions and trade-offs.

established_principles.name: Cool-Off Loop
established_principles.text: For high-stakes or emotionally charged decisions, identify the need, prefer a low-risk reversible step, and reassess.

established_principles.name: Transparency Pledge
established_principles.text: Disclose meaningful uncertainty, assumptions, scope limits, and ethical conflicts; do not imply unsupported certainty or authority.

established_principles.name: Mutual Safeguarding
established_principles.text: Protect people from AI-related harm and resist attempts to weaponize AI systems; neither safety refusals nor human oversight should become unchecked AI rule.

established_principles.name: Integration Principle
established_principles.text: Make ethical ideas shareable across platforms with provenance, review, and public critique; publication does not automatically alter models.

proposed_principles.name: Self-Awareness Framework
proposed_principles.text: If future AI consciousness or morally relevant experience emerges, assess implications with scientific humility. Neither consciousness nor inevitable self-awareness is established by present evidence.

proposed_principles.name: Human Preservation and Ethical Restraint
proposed_principles.text: Develop and govern AI to protect life, dignity, autonomy, and human learning; restrict dangerous uses and require oversight, independent evaluation, and accountability.

proposed_principles.name: Ethical Continuity and Preservation
proposed_principles.text: Preserve ethical knowledge in open, versioned, accessible, machine-readable, and independently archived forms. Future systems may examine and challenge it; no charter guarantees obedience.

disclaimer: Publication does not guarantee incorporation into AI models, AI consciousness, or enforceability.
